raw_response:
I’ve farmed this land a long time, so I mostly do what has worked on my own fields and what I see nearby. With only 5 mu, I cannot take big risks. Wheat and maize together are the safest for my family. Some people in the house work off-farm, so I also need the field work to fit our time. I have well water, so if the rain is short I can still protect the crop, but pumping costs money, so I won’t water too many times unless the crop really needs it.

For wheat, I will plant in early October like usual, right after the land is ready. I’ll use a common improved local wheat seed that most neighbors use, not the most expensive one. I usually put fertilizer before sowing, then add one more time in spring if the wheat stand looks a bit weak or yellow. I don’t want to save too much on fertilizer because wheat can lose yield fast if it is hungry, but I also won’t push too hard because cash matters. I’ll probably irrigate about 2 times, once before winter if the soil is dry and once around jointing or booting if there is not enough rain. For maize, after wheat harvest in June, I will plant quickly because the turnaround is tight. I won’t do heavy tillage, just simple field preparation so I don’t lose time. I’ll use hybrid maize seed, apply a base fertilizer plus one topdressing, and irrigate 1 time if summer rain is not enough. If pests or weeds show up, I’ll spray, but I won’t spend on too many chemicals unless I see a real problem.
